Repair: the first draft took Kent out of the whole 441-461 span, but the Kent page gives 'Established: c. 455', so the 9 cells of Kent's Cliopatria shape inside this shape are this state's until 455 (and the 19 cells of Deira's 555 shape until the Deira page's 'Established: c. 450'). ledger.note: 441: the Chronica Gallica of 452 records the British provinces passing to Saxon rule. 'The British provinces even at this time have been handed over across a wide area through various catastrophes and events to the rule of the Saxons.' The page names the year, not the land; the eastern arc is the settlement page's 'East Anglia, Lincolnshire, Essex and Kent'. The region is the whole Cliopatria shape because Deira and Kent, which the first draft cut out at once, are founded only in 450 and 455 (ledger below). The History of Anglo-Saxon England infobox gives 'Start of the Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain: c. 449' (Bede's date) and abandonment of Britannia in 410.

Infobox 'Established: c. 450'; 'The kingdom, which was previously ruled by a British dynasty, was probably created in the third quarter of the fifth century when Anglian warriors invaded the Derwent Valley'; 'Archaeology suggests that the Anglian royal house was in place by the middle of the fifth century, but the first certainly recorded king is Ælla in the late sixth century.' The kingdom-of-deira dossier of the group founds the kingdom c. 450 from this state and draws its 555 shape from then; 35 more cells of that shape come from the Britons (brythons dossier). The Chronicle's 449 landing at Ypwinesfleot (Ebbsfleet) comes earlier. Cliopatria keeps Kent inside the Anglo-Saxon shape until 490. The first draft gave the whole of region Kent to Kent from this state; only the 9 cells inside this state's shape are its to give, the rest being the Britons' (brythons ledger 455).

ledger.note: 480: Cliopatria widens the Anglo-Saxon shape by 144 cells, 89 of them once the Kent, Sussex and Deira land is left out; no page opened gives a date for it (page silent). The Sub-Roman Britain page says only that 'the British seem to have been in control of England and Wales roughly west of a line from York to Bournemouth' and that 'Until the 570s, Britons were still in control of about half of England and Wales'. Second page opened in the repair, Cerdic of Wessex: the Chronicle has Cerdic landing in 495 ('presumably in what is present-day Hampshire'), battles in 508 and 519, and the page warns 'The early history of Wessex in the Chronicle has been considered unreliable'; it also puts Mount Badon 'probably ... in 490 (and possibly later, but not later than 518)'. None of this dates a 144-cell growth in 480, so the event stays at Cliopatria's year, confidence 1. The first draft's 477 Sussex split is gone: Sussex was never this state's land before 480 (brythons ledger 477).

ledger.note: 527: the East Saxons' kingdom is established. Infobox 'Established: 527'; 'The first recorded king, according to the East Saxon King List, was Æscwine, to which a date of 527 is given'; 'It was founded in the 6th century and covered the territory later occupied by the counties of Essex, Middlesex,'; 'Saxon occupation of land that was to form the kingdom had begun by the early 5th century at Mucking and other locations.' The kingdom-of-essex dossier founds the kingdom in 527 from this state; Cliopatria's Essex row starts in 534, six years later, inside the 533 shape. The year is the page's (a king-list date, hence 2), the land the Essex dossier's reading.

ledger.note: 533: the one Anglo-Saxon shape is replaced by named kingdoms. Cliopatria ends the row in 533 and starts Mercia, Wessex, Deira and East Anglia in 534; none of the pages opened dates the step (page silent). The History of Anglo-Saxon England page: 'The most powerful included Northumbria, Mercia, East Anglia, Essex, Kent, Sussex, and Wessex' and 'Heptarchy (until 927)'. Second page opened in the repair, Heptarchy: 'The Heptarchy was the division of Anglo-Saxon England between the sixth and eighth centuries into petty kingdoms'; it gives no formation date for any kingdom. Of the 214 cells, 104 are in Cliopatria's Mercia 534, 41 in Wessex 534, 45 in East Anglia 534 (outside Essex), 5 in Deira 534 beyond the Deira dossier's shape, and 19 (Lincolnshire and the Fens, lat 52.7-53.7) in no 534 row.

wars.name: Hengist and Horsa's wars in Kent
wars.outcome: The Chronicle's Kentish campaign: 'in 455 Hengist and Horsa fought Vortigern at Ægelesthrep', where Horsa was killed; 'In 456 Hengest and Æsc battled the Britons at Crecganford'. Kent is established c. 455 and Hengist succeeded by Æsc.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article of this name; the wars are the Chronicle's entries as the Kent page reports them. The page treats the 449 landing in Kent as the Chronicle's date, with the dating of Bede's account 'semi-mythical' on the settlement page.

wars.name: Ælle's conquest of Sussex

zones.text: Mercredesburne (485) and the Saxon Shore fort of Andredadsceaster (491)

wars.outcome: 'Ælle's battle with the British in 485 near the bank of Mercredesburne', then 'his siege of the Saxon Shore fort at Andredadsceaster' 'in 491 after which the inhabitants were massacred'.
wars.note: The dates are the Chronicle's; 'Historians are divided over whether or not Ælle really existed' and the 477 base date may be 'about 20 years earlier'. Belligerents corrected in the repair: Sussex is the South Saxons' kingdom of its own (founded 477 from Brythons land), not part of this state.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line exists in the period; every edge of the Saxon-held land is an approximation from settlement archaeology and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle. The western edge is the least certain, the North Sea and Thames coasts the most.

notes: What this row is: Cliopatria's 'Anglo-Saxon England' (Seshat gb_anglo_saxon_1, not opened) is the Saxon-settled east of Britain before the named kingdoms of the 6th century, not a single state; the pages opened give it no capital, no rulers and no area, and the identity.capitals list is empty for that reason. Its start (441) rests on the Chronica Gallica entry for 441; its end (533) is only Cliopatria's hand-over to the Mercia, Wessex, Deira and East Anglia rows of 534 (page silent). Repair of 2026-10-25 (reviewer's five findings): (1) the 477 split to Sussex is deleted; Sussex lay wholly inside the Brythons shape (16 of 16 region cells) and passes to the kingdom of Sussex from the Britons in 477 (brythons ledger and keyframe brythons_477); the 480 correction removes region Sussex (16 cells), the land the Sussex dossier draws, from the 480 growth (the reviewer's wording was the whole Cliopatria Sussex row; the other 9 of its 23 cells, lat 50.8-51.2, lon -1.4 to 0.4, are kept here for 480-489 so that the 89-cell loss in the brythons ledger matches this gain; from 490 Cliopatria gives them to its Sussex row, which the Sussex dossier does not draw until its 661 gain, so they are in no dossier's shape 490-660: minor, for the Sussex author). (2) Kent is carved out only from 455 (Kent page 'Established: c. 455'): anglo-saxon-england_441 is ok, new keyframe anglo-saxon-england_455 carries the minus-Kent correction, and the found event now has the whole Cliopatria 441 shape; the 455 split is of the 9 Kent cells inside the shape (the other 9 are the Britons', brythons ledger 455). (3) East Anglia and Essex are not uncovered by Cliopatria: its rows Kingdom of East Anglia (52 cells) and Kingdom of Essex (16 cells) both start in 534 inside the 533 shape; only 19 cells of the 290 (Lincolnshire and the Fens) are in no 534 row. The successor for East Anglia now uses Cliopatria's row less the county of Essex, as the East Anglia dossier does. (4) Essex: the Essex page gives 'Established: 527', so a 527 split to kingdom-of-essex is added with keyframe anglo-saxon-england_527 (527-533) minus the Essex dossier's shape (the Cliopatria Essex row with the county of Essex, Southend-on-Sea and Thurrock, 24 cells); Essex is therefore no longer a successor at 533. (5) Deira: the Deira page gives 'Established: c. 450' and 'created in the third quarter of the fifth century', which matches the kingdom-of-deira dossier (found c. 450 from this state, 555 shape drawn from 450). The double claim is resolved in the Deira dossier's favour: a 450 split to kingdom-of-deira (19 cells inside this shape), new keyframe anglo-saxon-england_450, Deira taken out of the 490 and 523 shapes, and a matching 450 loss of 35 cells in the brythons dossier. Disagreement kept on the record: Cliopatria's own Deira row begins in 534 and the Deira page names no king before Ælla (559/560), so c. 450 rests on the infobox and on archaeology; if the orchestrator prefers 534, drop the 450 split, keyframes 450, 455 (Deira part), 462, 469, 480, 490, 523 and 527 (Deira part), and the Deira dossier's 450-533 keyframe; Deira would then be a plain successor again. Only 5 cells of Cliopatria's 534 Deira row are not in the Deira dossier's shape and are listed as the Deira successor. Still not settled: the 480 growth of 144 cells (the Cerdic of Wessex and Sub-Roman Britain pages date nothing in it; Cerdic's Chronicle landing is 495, Mount Badon 'probably ... 490') and the 533 hand-over (Heptarchy page: only 'between the sixth and eighth centuries'). Wihtgar/Wihtwara (Isle of Wight): the Wihtwara page gives 'in 534' for Wihtgar and Stuf receiving the island and Cliopatria starts the row in 523; the page was not opened here, so shape 523 is adjust only for Deira. The Chronicle dates for Wessex (495 Cerdic, 519) are on the Cerdic page now opened; the Wessex dossier should carry them. The History of Anglo-Saxon England infobox has no area, so the area ratio could not be taken for any shape. Pages: the first draft used 5; the repair opened Kingdom of Essex, Deira, Cerdic of Wessex and Heptarchy and re-read Kingdom of Kent and Kingdom of Sussex. Counterpart dossiers: brythons (this group), kingdom-of-kent, kingdom-of-sussex, kingdom-of-deira, kingdom-of-essex, kingdom-of-east-anglia, kingdom-of-mercia, kingdom-of-wessex all exist or are written by other parts of eu-11. Their founding events name different counterparts than the ones here: kingdom-of-kent /ledger/0 and kingdom-of-sussex /ledger/0 say 'nobody' where this dossier and the brythons dossier hand them land; kingdom-of-deira /ledger/0 names only anglo-saxon-england (35 of its cells come from brythons).
